findings.title: resolve() expiry check is inverted: deletes live links, serves expired ones
findings.description: resolve() removes the link and returns null when Instant.now().isBefore(link.expiresAt) — i.e. when the link is still VALID. Every freshly created link resolves to null and is permanently deleted from the store on first access, while already-expired links fall through, get their hits counted, and keep redirecting. This breaks the core feature and destroys data in normal use.

findings.title: create() throws NullPointerException on the first link of any owner
findings.description: quota.get(owner) returns null for an owner with no prior links, and `quota.get(owner) + 1` auto-unboxes that null, throwing NPE. Every owner's first POST /links crashes. Main.links() only catches IllegalArgumentException, so the exception escapes the handler and the client gets no response.

findings.title: verify() compares tokens with == so header-supplied tokens never match
findings.description: session.token == token is reference equality. Tokens arriving via HTTP are new String instances produced by header parsing/split, never the same object as the stored token, so verify() returns null for every legitimate request and every authenticated endpoint responds 401. The whole write and read surface is unusable.

findings.title: bearerToken() crashes on missing or malformed Authorization header
findings.description: Main.authenticate() passes getFirst("Authorization") straight in; if the header is absent, header.split(" ") throws NullPointerException, and if it has no space (e.g. just a raw token) parts[1] throws ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException. Any request without a well-formed 'Bearer x' header crashes the handler instead of returning 401.

findings.title: /stats divides by store.size(), throwing ArithmeticException on an empty store
findings.description: hits / store.size() performs integer division by zero whenever no links exist — i.e. on any fresh or fully-pruned server — so GET /stats throws and the client gets no response.

findings.title: page() sets end = size + 1, causing IndexOutOfBoundsException from subList
findings.description: When offset + size exceeds the list length, end is clamped to all.size() + 1 instead of all.size(). subList(offset, end) then throws IndexOutOfBoundsException. Any listing request whose page extends past the last link (e.g. default size 20 on a store with fewer links, when offset > 0, or the /report handler's page(0, 1000) once combined with a nonzero offset caller) crashes.

findings.title: Janitor removes from links map while iterating its keySet — ConcurrentModificationException kills the thread
findings.description: The janitor loop iterates store.all().keySet() and calls store.all().remove(code) inside the loop. HashMap's iterator is fail-fast, so the first tick that finds an expired link throws ConcurrentModificationException; the exception is uncaught in the Runnable, the janitor thread dies, and expired links are never swept again for the life of the process.

findings.title: sweep() removes entries while iterating keySet(), throwing ConcurrentModificationException
findings.description: sweep() iterates entries.keySet() and calls entries.remove(code) inside the loop; the first expired entry triggers ConcurrentModificationException. Since sweep() runs on the janitor tick, this exception propagates into the janitor thread and kills it, so neither cache nor store sweeping ever runs again.

findings.title: writeSnapshot ignores renameTo()'s result and stages in /tmp, silently losing snapshots
findings.description: File.renameTo returns false instead of throwing on failure, and its return value is discarded. Renames from /tmp into the export dir fail whenever the two are on different filesystems (the common case: /tmp is often tmpfs), so the snapshot is silently never written while the method claims durable success. A crash then recovers from a stale or missing snapshot.

findings.title: requireAdmin condition is a contradiction — every session is rejected, including admins
findings.description: !role.equals("admin") || !role.equals("owner") is true for every possible role (a string cannot equal both), so requireAdmin always returns false. Admins are locked out of anything gated by this check. Also NPEs if session is null.

findings.title: Bad LINKD_TIMEOUT_MS sets timeout to 0 while logging 'keeping default'
findings.description: On NumberFormatException the code prints 'keeping default' but then assigns cfg.timeoutMillis = 0, discarding the 10000ms default. validate() flags timeoutMillis <= 0 but returns true anyway, so the service starts with a zero timeout.

findings.title: validate() always returns true, so invalid configs start the service anyway
findings.description: The method collects problems and prints them, but unconditionally returns true. Its documented purpose — making a bad deploy fail at startup — never happens; an out-of-range port or zero timeout only produces a log line and the server proceeds (Main ignores the return value too, which this makes moot).

findings.title: LINKD_CACHE_TTL_MS (milliseconds) is stored directly into cacheTtlSeconds
findings.description: The doc comment says LINKD_CACHE_TTL_MS is a duration in milliseconds, but the parsed value is assigned to cacheTtlSeconds without dividing by 1000, making the effective cache TTL 1000x longer than configured. The Long.parseLong is also unguarded, so a malformed value crashes startup with an uncaught NumberFormatException (same for LINKD_CACHE_SIZE on line 54).

findings.title: LINKD_FETCH_LIMIT is parsed but never applied
findings.description: The parsed value is assigned to itself (parsed = parsed) and cfg.fetchLimit is never updated, so the environment variable is silently ignored and the fetch limit is always the default 32.

findings.title: byOwner() uses contains() instead of equals(), returning other owners' links
findings.description: link.owner.contains(owner) matches any owner whose name contains the query as a substring — byOwner("bob") returns bob's links plus bobby's. The doc promises 'exactly this owner', and Export.archiveAll-style per-owner handoffs built on this would include another user's data.

findings.title: findByCode() compares codes with == instead of equals()
findings.description: link.code == code is reference equality, so lookups with any code that isn't the identical interned String object return null even when a matching link exists.

findings.title: top() sorts ascending, returning the LEAST followed links
findings.description: Long.compare(a.hits, b.hits) sorts fewest-hits-first, then subList(0, n) takes the front of the list, so the 'leaderboard' returns the n least followed links instead of the most followed.

findings.title: extend() revives already-expired links, contradicting its documented contract
findings.description: The doc states an already-expired link stays expired, but the code unconditionally sets expiresAt = now + ttl, bringing dead codes back to life — exactly what the contract forbids.

findings.title: rename() validates 'from' twice and never validates 'to'
findings.description: Both validateCode calls pass `from`, so the new code `to` is stored without any validation — links can be renamed to empty, over-long, or invalid-character codes that validateCode is supposed to reject.

findings.title: importAll() is not atomic: a mid-batch validation failure leaves a partial import
findings.description: The doc promises all-or-nothing, but links are put into the map as they are validated. If the Nth link's code fails validateCode, the exception propagates with the first N-1 links already stored, leaving the store in exactly the half-imported state the contract rules out.

findings.title: successRate() uses integer division, reporting 0 unless every link was used
findings.description: used / links.size() is integer division that yields 0 whenever used < size, and only then multiplied by 100 — so the dashboard shows 0% for any partial usage and 100% only when every link has hits.

findings.title: utilization() integer division reports 0 until the cache is completely full
findings.description: entries.size() / limit is evaluated first as integer division, yielding 0 for any size below limit, then multiplied by 100 — the dashboard shows 0% at 99% occupancy. It also throws ArithmeticException if limit is 0 (Config only rejects negative cache sizes, so LINKD_CACHE_SIZE=0 reaches here).

findings.title: Eviction removes an arbitrary entry, not the least recently used one
findings.description: set() documents LRU eviction and get() maintains a `used` timestamp for that purpose, but eviction just removes the first key the HashMap iterator yields — an arbitrary entry unrelated to recency. Hot entries get evicted while stale ones survive, defeating the cache's stated policy.

findings.title: Link overrides equals() without hashCode(), breaking its documented use in sets and maps
findings.description: The class documents that links 'can be kept in sets and used as map keys', but overriding equals without hashCode violates the contract: two Links with the same code get different identity hash codes, so HashSet.contains / HashMap.get miss logically-equal links.

findings.title: warmCache() never shuts down its executor and returns before probes finish
findings.description: The doc says it 'returns after every probe has finished', but the method returns immediately after submit() with no shutdown()/awaitTermination(). Callers proceed against a cold cache, and each call leaks a fixed pool of 8 non-daemon threads for the life of the process — repeated calls grow thread count without bound.

findings.title: countForOwner() NPEs for owners with no links
findings.description: store.quotas().get(owner) returns null for an unknown owner, and returning it as int auto-unboxes null, throwing NullPointerException instead of the expected 0.

findings.title: /report without ?name exports links.csv but reads back null.csv
findings.description: exportCsv defaults a null name to "links" internally, but the handler's local `name` stays null, so readReport builds "null.csv", which doesn't exist — the request that just successfully wrote the report returns 500. The default (no-name) path always fails.

findings.title: Unvalidated Integer.parseInt on ttl/offset/size crashes handlers on bad input
findings.description: A non-numeric ?ttl= on POST /links (line 86), or non-numeric ?offset=/?size= on GET /links (lines 106-107), throws NumberFormatException outside any catch block; the handler dies without ever calling respond(), so the client gets no HTTP response instead of a 400.

findings.title: /l redirect NPEs when the code parameter is missing
findings.description: query(exchange).get("code") returns null when ?code= is absent, and code.toLowerCase() then throws NullPointerException, crashing the handler instead of returning 404/400.

findings.title: FileWriters not closed on exception in exportCsv and archiveAll
findings.description: writer.close() is only reached when write() succeeds; an IOException mid-write leaks the file handle (and in archiveAll aborts the loop leaving earlier handles' state uncertain). Under repeated failures handles accumulate.

findings.title: delete() never returns the owner's quota slot despite its documented contract
findings.description: The doc says deletion gives the owner their quota slot back, but the quota map is untouched, so per-owner counts on the admin dashboard drift upward forever and never reflect deletions.

findings.title: quotas() returns the live internal map, not the documented snapshot
findings.description: The doc states mutating the returned map must not affect the store, but the method returns the internal `quota` map itself — any caller mutation corrupts the store's quota accounting.

findings.title: newCode() can throw StringIndexOutOfBoundsException on short hex strings
findings.description: Long.toHexString produces fewer than 8 characters for values below 2^28, so substring(0, 8) occasionally (probability ~2^-36 per call) throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException, failing a create that should have succeeded.

findings.title: Metrics 'errors' counter is never incremented, so the dashboard always reports 0 errors
findings.description: snapshot() exposes an errors count and /stats renders it, but no code path ever increments `errors` — failures (400s, 500s, crashed handlers) are invisible on the dashboard, which permanently shows zero.

findings.title: Janitor removes store entries while iterating the keySet, killing the janitor thread with ConcurrentModificationException
findings.description: startJanitor iterates `store.all().keySet()` and calls `store.all().remove(code)` inside the loop. HashMap's keySet iterator is fail-fast: the first tick that finds an expired link (guaranteed within 30 days of any link's creation, and immediately for any short-TTL link) throws ConcurrentModificationException on the next iteration step. The exception is uncaught in the Runnable, so the janitor thread dies permanently — expired links are never swept again and Cache.sweep() at line 49 never runs either. This is deterministic and does not even require a second thread.

findings.title: Store's HashMap is mutated by the janitor thread and the HTTP handler thread with no synchronization
findings.description: Store has no synchronization at all, yet two threads use it concurrently: the HTTP dispatcher thread calls create/resolve/delete/page/totalHits, while the janitor thread (Worker.startJanitor) reads and removes entries via store.all(). Interleaving: the handler thread runs create() -> links.put(code, link) triggering a HashMap resize while the janitor thread runs links.get(code)/links.remove(code) — concurrent structural modification of an unsynchronized HashMap can lose entries, return null for present keys, throw spurious exceptions, or leave the table corrupted. page()'s `new ArrayList<>(links.values())` can likewise throw ConcurrentModificationException mid-copy when the janitor removes an entry. link.hits++ (line 45) and extend()'s expiresAt write are also plain non-atomic accesses with no happens-before edge to the janitor's reads of expiresAt.

findings.title: Cache.sweep removes entries while iterating keySet — ConcurrentModificationException despite being synchronized
findings.description: sweep() iterates `entries.keySet()` and calls `entries.remove(code)` inside the loop. `synchronized` protects against other threads but not against the fail-fast iterator: the first sweep that finds an expired entry throws ConcurrentModificationException on the following iteration step. Since sweep() is called from the janitor thread's loop with no exception handling, the janitor thread dies. Triggered deterministically once any cache entry has outlived cacheTtlSeconds (default 300s) at a janitor tick.

findings.title: Cache.peek, stats, and utilization read shared state without the lock the rest of the class relies on
findings.description: The class doc promises every method is safe from any number of threads, but peek() reads the HashMap unsynchronized, stats() reads `hits` unsynchronized, and utilization() reads entries.size() unsynchronized. Concrete interleaving today: the stats handler calls cache.utilization() on the dispatcher thread while the janitor thread runs synchronized sweep()/warm() mutating the map — an unsynchronized HashMap read concurrent with structural modification can return garbage or loop, and there is no visibility guarantee for `hits`. warm() is additionally a check-then-act race: peek() and set() are separate atomic sections, so an entry inserted by a handler between them is overwritten, resetting its LRU/TTL state.

findings.title: warmCache leaks a non-daemon thread pool per call and returns before the probes finish
findings.description: warmCache creates Executors.newFixedThreadPool(8), submits the tasks, and returns without shutdown() or awaitTermination(), despite its javadoc promising to return only after every probe has finished. Consequences: (1) the caller proceeds with a cache that is still cold — any logic sequenced after warmCache races the submitted tasks; (2) the pool's 8 non-daemon threads are never terminated, so each call permanently leaks 8 threads and a JVM that reaches a natural end of main-work can never exit.

findings.title: Metrics.addCreated is the only unsynchronized mutator in a class documented as safe for concurrent use
findings.description: addResolved() and snapshot() are synchronized but addCreated() increments `created` with no synchronization. created++ is a non-atomic read-modify-write with no happens-before edge to snapshot()'s read, so concurrent POST /links handlers lose increments and snapshot() can return stale values indefinitely. Today Main never sets an executor on HttpServer, so handlers happen to be serialized on the dispatcher thread — but the class contract says all methods are concurrency-safe, and the bug activates silently the moment an executor is configured or Metrics is touched from any second thread.

findings.title: Cache.getInstance is a non-thread-safe lazy singleton
findings.description: The check-then-act on the non-volatile static `instance` is unsynchronized: two threads calling getInstance concurrently can each observe null and construct separate Cache objects, and a non-null instance may be published without a happens-before edge, letting another thread see a partially initialized object. Today it is only called once from main() before any other thread exists, so this is latent — but it is exactly the pattern that breaks silently when a second call site appears.

findings.title: Session map is a plain HashMap shared across request handling with no synchronization
findings.description: issue() puts, revoke() removes, and verify() iterates sessions.values() with no locking. If HttpServer is ever given an executor (the normal production setup for this API), concurrent issue()+verify() means iterating a HashMap while it resizes — ConcurrentModificationException on login bursts, or corrupted lookups rejecting valid tokens. It is only safe today because Main never calls setExecutor, so all handlers run serially on the dispatcher thread; nothing in the code documents or enforces that assumption.

findings.title: Shared static SimpleDateFormat is not thread-safe
findings.description: SimpleDateFormat keeps mutable internal state (Calendar); concurrent STAMP.format() calls from two threads produce garbled timestamps or throw ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException. It is reached from the /report handler, which today runs serially on the single dispatcher thread, so the race is latent — it becomes real as soon as an executor is set on the server or Export is called from a background job.
